overview: This study note examines the reasons why Israel rejected the message, the remedy for that rejection, and the resulting consequences of their rejection. It explores the internal issues leading to their rejection, the necessary steps for belief, and the impact on the message shared with the Gentiles.

topics.title: Reasons for Rejection
topics.summary: Israel rejected the message because they did not feel a need for salvation, were zealous for God by making their own traditions, were proud and self-righteous, and misunderstood their law.
key_points: Did not feel need for salvation; thought they were fine, save themselves.
Made own traditions and worshipped them because they were zealous for God.
Were proud and self-righteous, refusing to listen and learn.
Misunderstood their own law; the law leads the sinner to the savior, and it must be obeyed in the heart as well.
Question raised: Is there a difference between obeying the Lord and calling on the Lord?

topics.title: Remedy for Rejection
topics.summary: The remedy for rejection involves using a missionary program and understanding that believing and obeying are not interchangeable, emphasizing that one must first hear.
key_points: Believing and obeying are not interchangeable.
To believe one must first hear.

topics.title: Results of Rejection
topics.summary: The rejection of Israel results in Israel being guilty, the message being shared with Gentiles, and God still yearning for His people.
key_points: Israel is guilty; Israel DID hear.
The message is shared with Gentiles due to Israel's rejection.
God still yearns for His people.
